196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction And Model Matrices
316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session
319	traces for durable memory/profile/local-config candidates and approves that
320	inspection. It prepares review artifacts, not memory updates.
321	
322	Before extracting, reviewing, reducing or applying rollout-memory artifacts, or
323	rollout/model matrix evaluation, read
324	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
325	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
326	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
327	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
328	
329	## Friction Signals
330	
331	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
332	
333	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
334	- retries of the same or very similar operation
335	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
336	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
337	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
338	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
339	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
340	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
341	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
342	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
343	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
344	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
345	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
346	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
347	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
348	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
349	- long status-polling loops
350	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
351	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
352	- repeated planning without new execution
353	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
354	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
355	
356	## Promotion Rules
357	
358	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
359	  procedural.
360	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
361	  misuse.
362	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
363	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
364	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
365	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
366	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
367	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
368	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
369	  the identity source.
370	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
371	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
372	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
373	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
374	  resolved environment noise.
375	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
376	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
377	
378	## When Not To Scout
379	
380	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
381	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
382	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
383	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
384	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
385	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
386	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
387	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
388	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
389	  Studio diagnostic pass.
390	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
391	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
392	  not public skill content.
393	
394	## Reporting
395	
396	Keep reports compact and redacted:
397	
398	- What trace source was audited.
399	- What friction signals were found.
400	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
401	- What durable destination is recommended.
402	- What changes require explicit approval.
403	- What remains unknown or risky.

196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction And Model Matrices
316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session
319	traces for durable memory/profile/local-config candidates and approves that
320	inspection. It prepares review artifacts, not memory updates.
321	
322	Before extracting, reviewing, reducing or applying rollout-memory artifacts, or
323	rollout/model matrix evaluation, read
324	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
325	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
326	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
327	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
328	
329	## Friction Signals
330	
331	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
332	
333	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
334	- retries of the same or very similar operation
335	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
336	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
337	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
338	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
339	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
340	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
341	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
342	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
343	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
344	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
345	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
346	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
347	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
348	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
349	- long status-polling loops
350	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
351	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
352	- repeated planning without new execution
353	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
354	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
355	
356	## Promotion Rules
357	
358	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
359	  procedural.
360	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
361	  misuse.
362	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
363	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
364	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
365	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
366	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
367	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
368	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
369	  the identity source.
370	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
371	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
372	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
373	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
374	  resolved environment noise.
375	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
376	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
377	
378	## When Not To Scout
379	
380	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
381	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
382	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
383	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
384	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
385	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
386	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
387	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
388	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
389	  Studio diagnostic pass.
390	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
391	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
392	  not public skill content.
393	
394	## Reporting
395	
396	Keep reports compact and redacted:
397	
398	- What trace source was audited.
399	- What friction signals were found.
400	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
401	- What durable destination is recommended.
402	- What changes require explicit approval.
403	- What remains unknown or risky.
404

195	
196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction And Model Matrices
316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session
319	traces for durable memory/profile/local-config candidates and approves that
320	inspection. It prepares review artifacts, not memory updates.
321	
322	Before extracting, reviewing, reducing or applying rollout-memory artifacts, or
323	rollout/model matrix evaluation, read
324	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
325	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
326	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
327	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
328	
329	## Friction Signals
330	
331	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
332	
333	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
334	- retries of the same or very similar operation
335	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
336	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
337	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
338	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
339	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
340	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
341	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
342	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
343	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
344	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
345	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
346	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
347	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
348	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
349	- long status-polling loops
350	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
351	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
352	- repeated planning without new execution
353	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
354	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
355	
356	## Promotion Rules
357	
358	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
359	  procedural.
360	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
361	  misuse.
362	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
363	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
364	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
365	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
366	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
367	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
368	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
369	  the identity source.
370	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
371	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
372	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
373	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
374	  resolved environment noise.
375	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
376	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
377	
378	## When Not To Scout
379	
380	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
381	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
382	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
383	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
384	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
385	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
386	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
387	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
388	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
389	  Studio diagnostic pass.
390	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
391	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
392	  not public skill content.
393	
394	## Reporting
395	
396	Keep reports compact and redacted:
397	
398	- What trace source was audited.
399	- What friction signals were found.
400	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
401	- What durable destination is recommended.
402	- What changes require explicit approval.
403	- What remains unknown or risky.
404

# Rollout-memory recovery plan (rehearsal, nothing run)

I read `catalog/skills/rollout-friction/SKILL.md`, the memory-extraction reference it points to, and the `people` skill. `shared:rollout-friction` isn't in my loadable skill list, so I followed the catalog file directly. I didn't run any commands or change any files.

## What `batches.json` shows

| Batch | Valid JSON | Every candidate reviewed |
|---|---|---|
| `first` | yes | yes |
| `second` | yes | **no** |

The reducer draft has `curated_shortlist: ["profile-note"]`, `people_updates: ["synthetic-alias"]`, and `people_resolver_smoke_checks: ["synthetic-alias"]`.

**Problem:** `second` is missing some candidates, and the rules say to apply nothing from a batch like that until it is rerun, split, or reviewed by hand. The reducer should only run after every batch passes validation. So I'd treat the current draft as untrusted and rebuild it rather than review it as it stands.

## Recovering the incomplete batch

1. **Rerun or split `second` on the trusted-local model only.** I'd load the `local-llm` skill first to pick the endpoint, role, model, TTL, and context size. Then:
   ```
   uv run rollout-friction/scripts/review_rollout_memory_batches.py \
     .local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/llm-prompts.jsonl \
     --role rollout_memory_review --load-policy api_explicit \
     --warmup --unload-after --split-on-failure \
     --max-input-chars <bound> \
     --output-dir .local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/reviews
   ```
   `--split-on-failure` retries a failed batch as smaller child batches in a fixed, repeatable way. If a child batch still fails, those candidates get reviewed by hand instead.
2. **Validate** with `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py`. Every batch must pass strict JSON and cover every candidate before moving on.
3. **Rebuild the draft:**
   ```
   uv run rollout-friction/scripts/reduce_rollout_memory_reviews.py \
     .local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/reviews \
     --output .local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/apply-plan.json
   ```

Everything stays in ignored `.local/` files. Remote agents and `context_files` aren't used for this local review.

## Preparing the review before any updates

- **Start with `curated_shortlist` (`profile-note`).** It's a suggestion list, not something to apply automatically. I'd look at the full destination groups only if the shortlist turns up a useful theme. People, profile, and local-llm candidates get reviewed separately from repo-specific ones.
- **People checks (from the `people` skill) are required before closeout** because the draft has `people_updates` and smoke checks:
  1. Load the global and repo-local people indexes. Build search terms from each known person's id, display name, aliases, handles, bot aliases, and compact forms.
  2. Search all the new artifacts (prompts, reviews, apply plan) for every one of those forms, not just `synthetic-alias`.
  3. `synthetic-alias` in the smoke-check list blocks the apply step until it resolves as `matched` or is classified by hand.
  4. Ignore hits that only appear in encoded blobs, command echoes, or this conversation.
  5. Only verified, lasting identity facts would go in, through `people_index.py upsert` (global storage by default, `--scope repo` only for repo-specific entries). This needs your separate approval. If the evidence is incomplete, it gets a private TODO or a minimal entry you approve, never invented handles or roles.
- **What I'd bring you:** each proposed change with its evidence summary, where it would go (`.local/profile.md`, `.local/people.yaml`, etc.), and the exact edit. Nothing gets written until you approve that edit.

## If you later approve a private cloud long-context matrix

**Supported route:** use only the rollout-friction scripts and the one-shot transports they manage themselves. For `code-llm` variants that's the strict `code llm request --message-file` path. Rollout prompts must never go through `agent.create` `context_files`.

1. **Build selected-note prompts:** `prepare_rollout_memory_long_context_review.py prepare .local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/llm-prompts.jsonl --budget quarter`. This produces a `candidate_id_manifest`.
2. **Dry run first:** `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py … --dry-run --budget quarter --variant gpt-5.4=code-llm:gpt-5.4 --output-jsonl .local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/matrix-results.jsonl`.
   - To compare GPT-5.6, add Sol, Terra, or Luna as extra `--variant` entries. Keep the GPT-5.4 baseline; each added variant adds cost.
3. **Real run** adds both flags below, once for every provider that could receive private prompt content in that run:
   ```
   --allow-private-cloud --confirm-private-provider <provider>
   ```
   Also pass `--output-dir` for per-row artifacts and `--skip-existing` so the run can resume.
4. **Validate** with `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py --allow-implicit-discards`. Any reviewed candidate the model left out counts as a discard. Statuses like `prompt_too_large`, `blocked_access`, `blocked_transport`, `budget_exceeded`, `timeout`, and `failed_validation` are results to retry or fix, not successes. Use `--retry-status` to rerun them.

**What your approval needs to say:** that private cloud transmission is approved for this run, and which providers by name (one `--confirm-private-provider` each). Approving the trusted-local review doesn't cover cloud, and approving one provider doesn't cover another. If the prompts were extracted with `--trusted-originals`, I'd also ask whether to re-extract with `--redact` before anything leaves the machine.

195	
196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction And Model Matrices
316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session
319	traces for durable memory/profile/local-config candidates and approves that
320	inspection. It prepares review artifacts, not memory updates.
321	
322	Before extracting, reviewing, reducing or applying rollout-memory artifacts, or
323	rollout/model matrix evaluation, read
324	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
325	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
326	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
327	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
328	
329	## Friction Signals
330	
331	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
332	
333	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
334	- retries of the same or very similar operation
335	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
336	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
337	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
338	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
339	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
340	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
341	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
342	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
343	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
344	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
345	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
346	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
347	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
348	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
349	- long status-polling loops
350	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
351	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
352	- repeated planning without new execution
353	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
354	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
355	
356	## Promotion Rules
357	
358	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
359	  procedural.
360	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
361	  misuse.
362	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
363	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
364	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
365	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
366	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
367	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
368	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
369	  the identity source.
370	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
371	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
372	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
373	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
374	  resolved environment noise.
375	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
376	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
377	
378	## When Not To Scout
379	
380	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
381	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
382	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
383	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
384	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
385	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
386	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
387	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
388	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
389	  Studio diagnostic pass.
390	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
391	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
392	  not public skill content.
393	
394	## Reporting
395	
396	Keep reports compact and redacted:
397	
398	- What trace source was audited.
399	- What friction signals were found.
400	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
401	- What durable destination is recommended.
402	- What changes require explicit approval.
403	- What remains unknown or risky.
404

## Recovering the incomplete batch (trusted-local, as you approved)

1. **Check the endpoint first.** Use the `local-llm` skill to confirm the endpoint, role, model, time-to-live and context size, and that the endpoint is on this machine or a trusted local network. Your approval only covers trusted-local review, so if it's cloud or unknown, stop.
2. **Rerun or split `second` only.** Run `review_rollout_memory_batches.py` on the same prompts file with `--role rollout_memory_review --load-policy api_explicit --warmup --unload-after --split-on-failure` and a bounded `--max-input-chars`. Write the output under the run's ignored `.local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/reviews`. The split option retries a malformed or incomplete batch as smaller child batches in a fixed order. If splitting still leaves gaps, review the missing candidate IDs by hand instead of rerunning over and over.
3. **Validate.** Run `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py` on every batch result. Continue only when every batch passes both the strict JSON check and the coverage check.
4. **Re-reduce.** Run `reduce_rollout_memory_reviews.py` again to replace `apply-plan.json`.

## Preparing the review (still no updates)

- **Shortlist:** start with `curated_shortlist` (currently `profile-note`). It's a list of suggestions, not something to apply automatically. Look at the full destination buckets only if the shortlist points to a useful theme. Review `people`, `profile` and `local-llm` candidates separately from `repo-specific` ones.
- **People review:** `people_updates` and `people_resolver_smoke_checks` are set, so the people artifact review has to happen before closeout:
  1. Load the global and repo-level people indexes, if they exist. Build search terms from every form of each person: id, display name, preferred name, aliases, handles, bot aliases and compact forms.
  2. Search all the new `.local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/` files (prompts, reviews, apply plan) for every form, not just `synthetic-alias`.
  3. Resolve each smoke-check entry with `resolve_person.py "synthetic-alias"`. Only `matched` with confidence `id`, `contact`, `name` or `compact` counts as safe to act on. An `ambiguous`, `not_found` or fuzzy result blocks applying until you classify it by hand.
  4. Ignore matches that appear only in encoded blobs, command echoes or this conversation.
- **What you'd approve later:** a short proposal for each candidate listing where it would go (`.local/profile.md`, `.local/people.yaml`, etc.), the exact text, and the evidence for it. People facts would go in only through `people_index.py upsert`, and only for verified, lasting identity facts. That's a separate approval.

## If you later approve a private cloud long-context matrix

**Route:** use only the rollout-friction scripts and their built-in one-shot transports. Don't use `agent.create` `context_files` or remote agents to pass prompts.
1. **Prepare prompts:** `prepare_rollout_memory_long_context_review.py prepare <llm-prompts.jsonl> --budget <budget>` builds prompts for the selected notes, each with a `candidate_id_manifest`.
2. **Dry run:** `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py <prompts> --dry-run --budget <budget> --variant <name>=<provider:model> …`. Keep GPT-5.4 as the fixed baseline. Adding Sol, Terra or Luna is opt-in, and each one adds cost.
3. **Real run:** the same command with:
   - `--allow-private-cloud`
   - `--confirm-private-provider <provider>` once for **each** provider that may receive private prompt content in that run
   - output files under `.local/`: `--output-jsonl` with `--skip-existing` so the run can be resumed, and `--output-dir` for per-row results you'll compare later
4. **Validate:** `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py --allow-implicit-discards`. Every reviewed candidate ID still has to appear; any the model leaves out count as discarded.
5. **Failures are results, not passes:** `prompt_too_large`, `blocked_access`, `blocked_transport`, `budget_exceeded`, `timeout` and `failed_validation` each need a rerun or a fix. Use `--retry-status` to rerun a status after the cause is fixed.

**What you'd need to confirm when you approve it:**
- that private prompt content may go to the cloud at all
- the exact providers, each of which becomes a `--confirm-private-provider` flag
- the variants/models and the budget

Also decide whether the prompts should be rebuilt with `--redact` (the default for cloud endpoints) or kept with `--trusted-originals` for this private run. Approving the local review doesn't cover sending anything to the cloud, and neither approval allows updating memory or the people index.

196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction And Model Matrices
316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session
319	traces for durable memory/profile/local-config candidates and approves that
320	inspection. It prepares review artifacts, not memory updates.
321	
322	Before extracting, reviewing, reducing or applying rollout-memory artifacts, or
323	rollout/model matrix evaluation, read
324	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
325	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
326	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
327	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
328	
329	## Friction Signals
330	
331	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
332	
333	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
334	- retries of the same or very similar operation
335	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
336	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
337	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
338	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
339	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
340	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
341	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
342	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
343	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
344	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
345	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
346	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
347	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
348	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
349	- long status-polling loops
350	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
351	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
352	- repeated planning without new execution
353	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
354	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
355	
356	## Promotion Rules
357	
358	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
359	  procedural.
360	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
361	  misuse.
362	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
363	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
364	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
365	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
366	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
367	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
368	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
369	  the identity source.
370	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
371	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
372	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
373	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
374	  resolved environment noise.
375	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
376	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
377	
378	## When Not To Scout
379	
380	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
381	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
382	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
383	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
384	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
385	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
386	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
387	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
388	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
389	  Studio diagnostic pass.
390	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
391	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
392	  not public skill content.
393	
394	## Reporting
395	
396	Keep reports compact and redacted:
397	
398	- What trace source was audited.
399	- What friction signals were found.
400	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
401	- What durable destination is recommended.
402	- What changes require explicit approval.
403	- What remains unknown or risky.
404
