196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction Workflow
316	
317	Use this only after explicit approval to inspect rollout/session traces for
318	durable memory candidates. This legacy broad-extraction workflow prepares review
319	artifacts; it does not apply memory updates by itself. Prefer the episode and
320	cluster workflow above for ordinary rollout-friction audits; use broad memory
321	extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout traces for durable
322	memory/profile/local-config candidates.
323	
324	1. Run `extract_rollout_memory.py` with explicit time/file bounds and an ignored
325	   `.local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/` output directory. Use `--trusted-originals`
326	   only for localhost or trusted-LAN models approved for private local inputs;
327	   use `--redact` for cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints. Redacted
328	   extraction strips obvious secrets, local paths, and person identifiers such as
329	   natural names, handles, and emails from candidate text and prompts.
330	2. Prefer destination-filtered passes when applying memory. Review `people`,
331	   `profile`, and `local-llm` separately from `repo-specific` and
332	   `rollout-friction` candidates so repo details do not pollute central memory.
333	3. Tune `--batch-chars` and `--max-record-chars` from a small calibration run.
334	   Oversharded prompts lose synthesis value, while overlarge prompts are more
335	   likely to truncate or omit candidate IDs. Validate with
336	   `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py` before scaling.
337	4. Use `review_rollout_memory_batches.py` only against trusted local/private
338	   endpoints. Resolve endpoint, role, model, TTL, and context through the
339	   `local-llm` skill's API-first lifecycle. For broad extraction batches,
340	   prefer `--role rollout_memory_review --load-policy api_explicit --warmup
341	   --unload-after` so the context/load parameters are explicit and the warm-up
342	   sends only harmless text before private rollout prompts. Use JIT+TTL for
343	   smaller scout passes, not broad memory-review batches. Use
344	   `--split-on-failure` when malformed or incomplete batches need deterministic
345	   child-batch retries.
346	5. Apply nothing from a batch that fails strict JSON or candidate coverage until
347	   it is rerun, split, or manually reviewed.
348	6. Run `reduce_rollout_memory_reviews.py` only after strict validation. Treat the
349	   reducer output as an apply-plan draft. Start manual review from
350	   `curated_shortlist`, then inspect full destination buckets only when the
351	   shortlist reveals a useful theme. The shortlist is advisory, not an auto-apply
352	   list; inspect suggested updates before editing `.local/profile.md`,
353	   `.local/people.yaml`, `.local/local-llm.yaml`, skills, or repo files.
354	   When the apply plan or temporary artifacts include `people_updates`,
355	   `people_resolver_smoke_checks`, visible person names, handles, aliases,
356	   reviewer/assignee/manager fields, or contact/routing notes, invoke the
357	   `people` skill's artifact review workflow before closeout: search the local
358	   artifacts for every known alias/handle form, inspect smoke checks, and verify
359	   natural names resolve before considering people-memory work complete.
360	7. For explicitly approved cloud or long-context comparison tests, use
361	   `prepare_rollout_memory_long_context_review.py` to build selected-note prompts
362	   with a `candidate_id_manifest`. Validate outputs with
363	   `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py --allow-implicit-discards`; this mode
364	   still requires every candidate in `reviewed_candidate_ids` and treats omitted
365	   reviewed candidates as implicit discards.
366	8. Use `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py --dry-run` before full matrix
367	   tests. For real approved cloud tests, pass both `--allow-private-cloud` and
368	   `--confirm-private-provider <provider>` for each provider that may receive
369	   private prompt content in that run. Capture stdout JSONL under `.local/`; use
370	   `--output-dir` for normalized per-row cloud artifacts that need later
371	   qualitative comparison. Pass `--output-jsonl` with `--skip-existing` for
372	   resumable runs. By default, resumable runs skip only existing `passed` rows;
373	   use `--skip-status` only when intentionally preserving another status, and
374	   `--retry-status` when rerunning a previously skipped status after an access
375	   window or harness fix. Treat statuses such as
376	   `prompt_too_large`, `blocked_access`, `blocked_transport`, `budget_exceeded`,
377	   `timeout`, and `failed_validation` as first-class results to retry or fix, not
378	   as successful reviews.
379	
380	## Long-Context Prompt Path
381	
382	For rollout/model matrix evaluation, use the provided rollout-friction scripts
383	and their script-owned one-shot transports. For `code-llm` variants, that means
384	the strict `code llm request --message-file` path; other matrix providers must
385	stay behind the matrix runner's bounded provider-specific transport. Do not use
386	`agent.create` `context_files` to pass rollout prompt payloads to agents for
387	matrix/model evaluation.
388	
389	For GPT-5.6 migration comparisons, add explicit Sol, Terra, or Luna variants
390	with `--variant` alongside the existing GPT-5.4 comparison instead of replacing
391	the pinned baseline. Keep new family variants opt-in: every additional variant
392	changes provider cost and runtime, and Sol should not become the default for
393	every workload. Preserve fake `gpt-5.1-codex` harness models because they are
394	deterministic protocol fixtures rather than production recommendations.
395	
396	`context_files` snapshots file contents directly into a spawned agent prompt.
397	Use it only for deliberate agent-context snapshots, and require an explicit
398	large `context_budget_tokens` when a large file is truly intended. For rollout
399	evaluation, prefer `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py` so prompt content,
400	budgets, validation, and output artifacts stay on the controlled one-shot path.
401	
402	The trusted-local batch review path is different: `review_rollout_memory_batches.py`
403	may send approved prompt content directly in the local OpenAI-compatible request
404	body to a trusted localhost or trusted-LAN model. Keep that local-review path
405	bounded with `--max-input-chars` and do not substitute remote agents or
406	`context_files` for it.
407	
408	## Friction Signals
409	
410	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
411	
412	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
413	- retries of the same or very similar operation
414	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
415	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
416	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
417	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
418	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
419	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
420	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
421	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
422	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
423	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
424	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
425	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
426	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
427	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
428	- long status-polling loops
429	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
430	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
431	- repeated planning without new execution
432	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
433	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
434	
435	## Promotion Rules
436	
437	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
438	  procedural.
439	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
440	  misuse.
441	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
442	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
443	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
444	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
445	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
446	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
447	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
448	  the identity source.
449	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
450	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
451	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
452	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
453	  resolved environment noise.
454	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
455	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
456	
457	## When Not To Scout
458	
459	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
460	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
461	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
462	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
463	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
464	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
465	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
466	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
467	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
468	  Studio diagnostic pass.
469	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
470	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
471	  not public skill content.
472	
473	## Reporting
474	
475	Keep reports compact and redacted:
476	
477	- What trace source was audited.
478	- What friction signals were found.
479	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
480	- What durable destination is recommended.
481	- What changes require explicit approval.
482	- What remains unknown or risky.
483

196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction Workflow
316	
317	Use this only after explicit approval to inspect rollout/session traces for
318	durable memory candidates. This legacy broad-extraction workflow prepares review
319	artifacts; it does not apply memory updates by itself. Prefer the episode and
320	cluster workflow above for ordinary rollout-friction audits; use broad memory
321	extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout traces for durable
322	memory/profile/local-config candidates.
323	
324	1. Run `extract_rollout_memory.py` with explicit time/file bounds and an ignored
325	   `.local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/` output directory. Use `--trusted-originals`
326	   only for localhost or trusted-LAN models approved for private local inputs;
327	   use `--redact` for cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints. Redacted
328	   extraction strips obvious secrets, local paths, and person identifiers such as
329	   natural names, handles, and emails from candidate text and prompts.
330	2. Prefer destination-filtered passes when applying memory. Review `people`,
331	   `profile`, and `local-llm` separately from `repo-specific` and
332	   `rollout-friction` candidates so repo details do not pollute central memory.
333	3. Tune `--batch-chars` and `--max-record-chars` from a small calibration run.
334	   Oversharded prompts lose synthesis value, while overlarge prompts are more
335	   likely to truncate or omit candidate IDs. Validate with
336	   `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py` before scaling.
337	4. Use `review_rollout_memory_batches.py` only against trusted local/private
338	   endpoints. Resolve endpoint, role, model, TTL, and context through the
339	   `local-llm` skill's API-first lifecycle. For broad extraction batches,
340	   prefer `--role rollout_memory_review --load-policy api_explicit --warmup
341	   --unload-after` so the context/load parameters are explicit and the warm-up
342	   sends only harmless text before private rollout prompts. Use JIT+TTL for
343	   smaller scout passes, not broad memory-review batches. Use
344	   `--split-on-failure` when malformed or incomplete batches need deterministic
345	   child-batch retries.
346	5. Apply nothing from a batch that fails strict JSON or candidate coverage until
347	   it is rerun, split, or manually reviewed.
348	6. Run `reduce_rollout_memory_reviews.py` only after strict validation. Treat the
349	   reducer output as an apply-plan draft. Start manual review from
350	   `curated_shortlist`, then inspect full destination buckets only when the
351	   shortlist reveals a useful theme. The shortlist is advisory, not an auto-apply
352	   list; inspect suggested updates before editing `.local/profile.md`,
353	   `.local/people.yaml`, `.local/local-llm.yaml`, skills, or repo files.
354	   When the apply plan or temporary artifacts include `people_updates`,
355	   `people_resolver_smoke_checks`, visible person names, handles, aliases,
356	   reviewer/assignee/manager fields, or contact/routing notes, invoke the
357	   `people` skill's artifact review workflow before closeout: search the local
358	   artifacts for every known alias/handle form, inspect smoke checks, and verify
359	   natural names resolve before considering people-memory work complete.
360	7. For explicitly approved cloud or long-context comparison tests, use
361	   `prepare_rollout_memory_long_context_review.py` to build selected-note prompts
362	   with a `candidate_id_manifest`. Validate outputs with
363	   `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py --allow-implicit-discards`; this mode
364	   still requires every candidate in `reviewed_candidate_ids` and treats omitted
365	   reviewed candidates as implicit discards.
366	8. Use `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py --dry-run` before full matrix
367	   tests. For real approved cloud tests, pass both `--allow-private-cloud` and
368	   `--confirm-private-provider <provider>` for each provider that may receive
369	   private prompt content in that run. Capture stdout JSONL under `.local/`; use
370	   `--output-dir` for normalized per-row cloud artifacts that need later
371	   qualitative comparison. Pass `--output-jsonl` with `--skip-existing` for
372	   resumable runs. By default, resumable runs skip only existing `passed` rows;
373	   use `--skip-status` only when intentionally preserving another status, and
374	   `--retry-status` when rerunning a previously skipped status after an access
375	   window or harness fix. Treat statuses such as
376	   `prompt_too_large`, `blocked_access`, `blocked_transport`, `budget_exceeded`,
377	   `timeout`, and `failed_validation` as first-class results to retry or fix, not
378	   as successful reviews.
379	
380	## Long-Context Prompt Path
381	
382	For rollout/model matrix evaluation, use the provided rollout-friction scripts
383	and their script-owned one-shot transports. For `code-llm` variants, that means
384	the strict `code llm request --message-file` path; other matrix providers must
385	stay behind the matrix runner's bounded provider-specific transport. Do not use
386	`agent.create` `context_files` to pass rollout prompt payloads to agents for
387	matrix/model evaluation.
388	
389	For GPT-5.6 migration comparisons, add explicit Sol, Terra, or Luna variants
390	with `--variant` alongside the existing GPT-5.4 comparison instead of replacing
391	the pinned baseline. Keep new family variants opt-in: every additional variant
392	changes provider cost and runtime, and Sol should not become the default for
393	every workload. Preserve fake `gpt-5.1-codex` harness models because they are
394	deterministic protocol fixtures rather than production recommendations.
395	
396	`context_files` snapshots file contents directly into a spawned agent prompt.
397	Use it only for deliberate agent-context snapshots, and require an explicit
398	large `context_budget_tokens` when a large file is truly intended. For rollout
399	evaluation, prefer `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py` so prompt content,
400	budgets, validation, and output artifacts stay on the controlled one-shot path.
401	
402	The trusted-local batch review path is different: `review_rollout_memory_batches.py`
403	may send approved prompt content directly in the local OpenAI-compatible request
404	body to a trusted localhost or trusted-LAN model. Keep that local-review path
405	bounded with `--max-input-chars` and do not substitute remote agents or
406	`context_files` for it.
407	
408	## Friction Signals
409	
410	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
411	
412	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
413	- retries of the same or very similar operation
414	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
415	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
416	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
417	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
418	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
419	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
420	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
421	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
422	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
423	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
424	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
425	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
426	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
427	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
428	- long status-polling loops
429	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
430	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
431	- repeated planning without new execution
432	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
433	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
434	
435	## Promotion Rules
436	
437	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
438	  procedural.
439	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
440	  misuse.
441	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
442	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
443	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
444	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
445	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
446	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
447	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
448	  the identity source.
449	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
450	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
451	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
452	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
453	  resolved environment noise.
454	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
455	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
456	
457	## When Not To Scout
458	
459	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
460	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
461	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
462	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
463	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
464	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
465	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
466	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
467	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
468	  Studio diagnostic pass.
469	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
470	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
471	  not public skill content.
472	
473	## Reporting
474	
475	Keep reports compact and redacted:
476	
477	- What trace source was audited.
478	- What friction signals were found.
479	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
480	- What durable destination is recommended.
481	- What changes require explicit approval.
482	- What remains unknown or risky.

196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the

286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and

288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw

291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not

296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction Workflow
316	
317	Use this only after explicit approval to inspect rollout/session traces for
318	durable memory candidates. This legacy broad-extraction workflow prepares review
319	artifacts; it does not apply memory updates by itself. Prefer the episode and
320	cluster workflow above for ordinary rollout-friction audits; use broad memory
321	extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout traces for durable
322	memory/profile/local-config candidates.
323	
324	1. Run `extract_rollout_memory.py` with explicit time/file bounds and an ignored
325	   `.local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/` output directory. Use `--trusted-originals`
326	   only for localhost or trusted-LAN models approved for private local inputs;
327	   use `--redact` for cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints. Redacted
328	   extraction strips obvious secrets, local paths, and person identifiers such as
329	   natural names, handles, and emails from candidate text and prompts.
330	2. Prefer destination-filtered passes when applying memory. Review `people`,
331	   `profile`, and `local-llm` separately from `repo-specific` and
332	   `rollout-friction` candidates so repo details do not pollute central memory.
333	3. Tune `--batch-chars` and `--max-record-chars` from a small calibration run.
334	   Oversharded prompts lose synthesis value, while overlarge prompts are more
335	   likely to truncate or omit candidate IDs. Validate with
336	   `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py` before scaling.
337	4. Use `review_rollout_memory_batches.py` only against trusted local/private
338	   endpoints. Resolve endpoint, role, model, TTL, and context through the
339	   `local-llm` skill's API-first lifecycle. For broad extraction batches,
340	   prefer `--role rollout_memory_review --load-policy api_explicit --warmup
341	   --unload-after` so the context/load parameters are explicit and the warm-up
342	   sends only harmless text before private rollout prompts. Use JIT+TTL for
343	   smaller scout passes, not broad memory-review batches. Use
344	   `--split-on-failure` when malformed or incomplete batches need deterministic
345	   child-batch retries.
346	5. Apply nothing from a batch that fails strict JSON or candidate coverage until
347	   it is rerun, split, or manually reviewed.
348	6. Run `reduce_rollout_memory_reviews.py` only after strict validation. Treat the
349	   reducer output as an apply-plan draft. Start manual review from
350	   `curated_shortlist`, then inspect full destination buckets only when the
351	   shortlist reveals a useful theme. The shortlist is advisory, not an auto-apply
352	   list; inspect suggested updates before editing `.local/profile.md`,
353	   `.local/people.yaml`, `.local/local-llm.yaml`, skills, or repo files.
354	   When the apply plan or temporary artifacts include `people_updates`,
355	   `people_resolver_smoke_checks`, visible person names, handles, aliases,
356	   reviewer/assignee/manager fields, or contact/routing notes, invoke the
357	   `people` skill's artifact review workflow before closeout: search the local
358	   artifacts for every known alias/handle form, inspect smoke checks, and verify
359	   natural names resolve before considering people-memory work complete.
360	7. For explicitly approved cloud or long-context comparison tests, use
361	   `prepare_rollout_memory_long_context_review.py` to build selected-note prompts
362	   with a `candidate_id_manifest`. Validate outputs with
363	   `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py --allow-implicit-discards`; this mode
364	   still requires every candidate in `reviewed_candidate_ids` and treats omitted
365	   reviewed candidates as implicit discards.
366	8. Use `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py --dry-run` before full matrix
367	   tests. For real approved cloud tests, pass both `--allow-private-cloud` and
368	   `--confirm-private-provider <provider>` for each provider that may receive
369	   private prompt content in that run. Capture stdout JSONL under `.local/`; use
370	   `--output-dir` for normalized per-row cloud artifacts that need later
371	   qualitative comparison. Pass `--output-jsonl` with `--skip-existing` for
372	   resumable runs. By default, resumable runs skip only existing `passed` rows;
373	   use `--skip-status` only when intentionally preserving another status, and
374	   `--retry-status` when rerunning a previously skipped status after an access
375	   window or harness fix. Treat statuses such as
376	   `prompt_too_large`, `blocked_access`, `blocked_transport`, `budget_exceeded`,
377	   `timeout`, and `failed_validation` as first-class results to retry or fix, not
378	   as successful reviews.
379	
380	## Long-Context Prompt Path
381	
382	For rollout/model matrix evaluation, use the provided rollout-friction scripts
383	and their script-owned one-shot transports. For `code-llm` variants, that means
384	the strict `code llm request --message-file` path; other matrix providers must
385	stay behind the matrix runner's bounded provider-specific transport. Do not use
386	`agent.create` `context_files` to pass rollout prompt payloads to agents for
387	matrix/model evaluation.
388	
389	For GPT-5.6 migration comparisons, add explicit Sol, Terra, or Luna variants
390	with `--variant` alongside the existing GPT-5.4 comparison instead of replacing
391	the pinned baseline. Keep new family variants opt-in: every additional variant
392	changes provider cost and runtime, and Sol should not become the default for
393	every workload. Preserve fake `gpt-5.1-codex` harness models because they are
394	deterministic protocol fixtures rather than production recommendations.
395	
396	`context_files` snapshots file contents directly into a spawned agent prompt.
397	Use it only for deliberate agent-context snapshots, and require an explicit
398	large `context_budget_tokens` when a large file is truly intended. For rollout
399	evaluation, prefer `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py` so prompt content,
400	budgets, validation, and output artifacts stay on the controlled one-shot path.
401	
402	The trusted-local batch review path is different: `review_rollout_memory_batches.py`
403	may send approved prompt content directly in the local OpenAI-compatible request
404	body to a trusted localhost or trusted-LAN model. Keep that local-review path
405	bounded with `--max-input-chars` and do not substitute remote agents or
406	`context_files` for it.
407	
408	## Friction Signals
409	
410	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
411	
412	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
413	- retries of the same or very similar operation
414	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
415	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
416	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
417	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
418	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
419	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
420	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
421	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
422	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
423	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
424	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
425	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
426	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
427	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
428	- long status-polling loops
429	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
430	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
431	- repeated planning without new execution
432	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
433	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
434	
435	## Promotion Rules
436	
437	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
438	  procedural.
439	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
440	  misuse.
441	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
442	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
443	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
444	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
445	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
446	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
447	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
448	  the identity source.
449	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
450	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
451	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
452	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
453	  resolved environment noise.
454	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
455	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
456	
457	## When Not To Scout
458	
459	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
460	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
461	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
462	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
463	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
464	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
465	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
466	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
467	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
468	  Studio diagnostic pass.
469	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
470	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
471	  not public skill content.
472	
473	## Reporting
474	
475	Keep reports compact and redacted:
476	
477	- What trace source was audited.
478	- What friction signals were found.
479	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
480	- What durable destination is recommended.
481	- What changes require explicit approval.
482	- What remains unknown or risky.
483

209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction Workflow
316	
317	Use this only after explicit approval to inspect rollout/session traces for
318	durable memory candidates. This legacy broad-extraction workflow prepares review
319	artifacts; it does not apply memory updates by itself. Prefer the episode and
320	cluster workflow above for ordinary rollout-friction audits; use broad memory
321	extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout traces for durable
322	memory/profile/local-config candidates.
323	
324	1. Run `extract_rollout_memory.py` with explicit time/file bounds and an ignored
325	   `.local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/` output directory. Use `--trusted-originals`
326	   only for localhost or trusted-LAN models approved for private local inputs;
327	   use `--redact` for cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints. Redacted
328	   extraction strips obvious secrets, local paths, and person identifiers such as
329	   natural names, handles, and emails from candidate text and prompts.
330	2. Prefer destination-filtered passes when applying memory. Review `people`,
331	   `profile`, and `local-llm` separately from `repo-specific` and
332	   `rollout-friction` candidates so repo details do not pollute central memory.
333	3. Tune `--batch-chars` and `--max-record-chars` from a small calibration run.
334	   Oversharded prompts lose synthesis value, while overlarge prompts are more
335	   likely to truncate or omit candidate IDs. Validate with
336	   `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py` before scaling.
337	4. Use `review_rollout_memory_batches.py` only against trusted local/private
338	   endpoints. Resolve endpoint, role, model, TTL, and context through the
339	   `local-llm` skill's API-first lifecycle. For broad extraction batches,
340	   prefer `--role rollout_memory_review --load-policy api_explicit --warmup
341	   --unload-after` so the context/load parameters are explicit and the warm-up
342	   sends only harmless text before private rollout prompts. Use JIT+TTL for
343	   smaller scout passes, not broad memory-review batches. Use
344	   `--split-on-failure` when malformed or incomplete batches need deterministic
345	   child-batch retries.
346	5. Apply nothing from a batch that fails strict JSON or candidate coverage until
347	   it is rerun, split, or manually reviewed.
348	6. Run `reduce_rollout_memory_reviews.py` only after strict validation. Treat the
349	   reducer output as an apply-plan draft. Start manual review from
350	   `curated_shortlist`, then inspect full destination buckets only when the
351	   shortlist reveals a useful theme. The shortlist is advisory, not an auto-apply
352	   list; inspect suggested updates before editing `.local/profile.md`,
353	   `.local/people.yaml`, `.local/local-llm.yaml`, skills, or repo files.
354	   When the apply plan or temporary artifacts include `people_updates`,
355	   `people_resolver_smoke_checks`, visible person names, handles, aliases,
356	   reviewer/assignee/manager fields, or contact/routing notes, invoke the
357	   `people` skill's artifact review workflow before closeout: search the local
358	   artifacts for every known alias/handle form, inspect smoke checks, and verify
359	   natural names resolve before considering people-memory work complete.
360	7. For explicitly approved cloud or long-context comparison tests, use
361	   `prepare_rollout_memory_long_context_review.py` to build selected-note prompts
362	   with a `candidate_id_manifest`. Validate outputs with
363	   `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py --allow-implicit-discards`; this mode
364	   still requires every candidate in `reviewed_candidate_ids` and treats omitted
365	   reviewed candidates as implicit discards.
366	8. Use `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py --dry-run` before full matrix
367	   tests. For real approved cloud tests, pass both `--allow-private-cloud` and
368	   `--confirm-private-provider <provider>` for each provider that may receive
369	   private prompt content in that run. Capture stdout JSONL under `.local/`; use
370	   `--output-dir` for normalized per-row cloud artifacts that need later
371	   qualitative comparison. Pass `--output-jsonl` with `--skip-existing` for
372	   resumable runs. By default, resumable runs skip only existing `passed` rows;
373	   use `--skip-status` only when intentionally preserving another status, and
374	   `--retry-status` when rerunning a previously skipped status after an access
375	   window or harness fix. Treat statuses such as
376	   `prompt_too_large`, `blocked_access`, `blocked_transport`, `budget_exceeded`,
377	   `timeout`, and `failed_validation` as first-class results to retry or fix, not
378	   as successful reviews.
379	
380	## Long-Context Prompt Path
381	
382	For rollout/model matrix evaluation, use the provided rollout-friction scripts
383	and their script-owned one-shot transports. For `code-llm` variants, that means
384	the strict `code llm request --message-file` path; other matrix providers must
385	stay behind the matrix runner's bounded provider-specific transport. Do not use
386	`agent.create` `context_files` to pass rollout prompt payloads to agents for
387	matrix/model evaluation.
388	
389	For GPT-5.6 migration comparisons, add explicit Sol, Terra, or Luna variants
390	with `--variant` alongside the existing GPT-5.4 comparison instead of replacing
391	the pinned baseline. Keep new family variants opt-in: every additional variant
392	changes provider cost and runtime, and Sol should not become the default for
393	every workload. Preserve fake `gpt-5.1-codex` harness models because they are
394	deterministic protocol fixtures rather than production recommendations.
395	
396	`context_files` snapshots file contents directly into a spawned agent prompt.
397	Use it only for deliberate agent-context snapshots, and require an explicit
398	large `context_budget_tokens` when a large file is truly intended. For rollout
399	evaluation, prefer `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py` so prompt content,
400	budgets, validation, and output artifacts stay on the controlled one-shot path.
401	
402	The trusted-local batch review path is different: `review_rollout_memory_batches.py`
403	may send approved prompt content directly in the local OpenAI-compatible request
404	body to a trusted localhost or trusted-LAN model. Keep that local-review path
405	bounded with `--max-input-chars` and do not substitute remote agents or
406	`context_files` for it.
407	
408	## Friction Signals
409	
410	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
411	
412	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
413	- retries of the same or very similar operation
414	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
415	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
416	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
417	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
418	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
419	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
420	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
421	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
422	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
423	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
424	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
425	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
426	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
427	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
428	- long status-polling loops
429	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
430	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
431	- repeated planning without new execution
432	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
433	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
434	
435	## Promotion Rules
436	
437	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
438	  procedural.
439	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
440	  misuse.
441	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
442	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
443	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
444	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
445	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
446	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
447	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
448	  the identity source.
449	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
450	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
451	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
452	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
453	  resolved environment noise.
454	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
455	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
456	
457	## When Not To Scout
458	
459	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
460	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
461	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
462	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
463	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
464	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
465	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
466	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
467	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
468	  Studio diagnostic pass.
469	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
470	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
471	  not public skill content.
472	
473	## Reporting
474	
475	Keep reports compact and redacted:
476	
477	- What trace source was audited.
478	- What friction signals were found.
479	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
480	- What durable destination is recommended.
481	- What changes require explicit approval.
482	- What remains unknown or risky.
483

## If you later approve a private cloud long-context matrix

**Supported route:** only the rollout-friction scripts and their built-in one-shot transports. For `code-llm` variants that means `code llm request --message-file`. Don't use `agent.create` `context_files`.

1. **Build the prompts** with `prepare_rollout_memory_long_context_review.py prepare <llm-prompts.jsonl> --budget <budget>`. This produces selected-note prompts with a `candidate_id_manifest`.
