    description: Optional details_file prefix resolved under the matched index scope's private `.local/` root.
---

# People

Resolve identity, aliases/bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces,
company/team/title, private profile notes, and trust/relationship hints. This
private layer does not decide workflow ownership: `github-plan` owns planning
routing, for example. Repo metadata keeps public-safe behavior such as docs,
gates, health, cleanup and conceptual product ownership.

## Optional Private Storage

Durable identity context defaults to global/user storage:
`$CODE_HOME/skills/.local/people.yaml`, with details in
`$CODE_HOME/skills/.local/people/<person-id>.md`. Helpers fall back from
`CODE_HOME` to `CODEX_HOME`, then `~/.code`; if none exists (for example on a
catalog-only host), they use `.local/` inside the catalog shipping the helper.

Repo-local `.local/people.yaml` and `.local/people/<person-id>.md` are overlays
for project-specific contacts, client context, overrides or supplements. The
resolver loads global entries first, then repo entries: the same `id` replaces
the global entry for that repo; new ids supplement it. Missing indexes are
normal: continue without enrichment, not an error.

Use [the public-safe schema](references/people.local.example.yaml) for the
optional gitignored index. Real names, handles, emails, phone numbers, company
and relationship facts belong only in ignored local files. Update through
`uv run people/scripts/people_index.py upsert --id <id> --display-name "<name>" --github <handle>`, which
defaults to global/user storage; use `--scope repo` only for repo-specific
people/overrides/supplements. Read [migration](references/migration.md) before
consolidating identity facts from other local sources.

## Resolve Before Relying On Identity

1. Resolve each named human reference when context may matter, using the helper
   from this skill directory:

   ```sh
   uv run people/scripts/resolve_person.py "<name-or-handle>"
   ```

2. Branch on `status`: `matched` permits task-relevant fields; `ambiguous`
   requires a short clarification before relying on person-specific context;
   `not_found` or `no_index` means proceed without enrichment. Load a linked
   detail file only after one person resolves and richer context is needed.
3. For assigning, mentioning, routing, commenting or other writes, only
   `matched` with confidence `id`, `contact`, `name` or `compact` is write-safe
   identity context. Fuzzy, ambiguous and unknown-confidence results are
   lookup-only. Prefer configured aliases/handles over guessing.
4. Treat actors not resolved to a known person or configured bot alias as
   unknown: verify claims from live evidence, do not assume intent/authority,
   and state uncertainty when it affects the work. Local trust hints guide
   caution and verification; never use them to skip live checks.

The resolver trims whitespace, strips leading `@`, case-folds, normalizes
Unicode/collapses whitespace, and compares compact forms ignoring spaces,
dots, hyphens and underscores. Tiers in order: exact normalized id or
`person:<id>`; contact handles (GitHub/Slack/Discord/email/other keys); display
name/preferred reference/alias/known misspelling; compact exact match; optional
conservative fuzzy matching only when explicitly requested and one candidate
is obvious. A tie at the winning tier returns `ambiguous`, omitting notes and
detail files.

Refresh the private index when artifact review or live evidence shows verified
durable renames, handles, role/relationship corrections or repeatedly unresolved
natural names that should resolve. Keep useful former spellings as aliases; do not call
an old alias stale without user or maintained-source confirmation.

## Artifact Review Workflow

When `memory-distillation` or `rollout-friction` creates ignored local artifacts
such as `.local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/`, `.local/scan-output/<run-id>/`,
apply plans, reducer inputs, prompts, or reviewed batch results, use this skill
to review those artifacts for person facts before closeout if any artifact has
`people_updates`, `people_resolver_smoke_checks`, or visible person names,
handles, aliases, reviewer/assignee/manager fields, or contact/routing notes.

1. Load the small global/user and repo-local people indexes when available, and
   build search terms from each known person's id, display name, preferred
   reference, aliases, handles, bot aliases, and compact forms.
2. Search the new local artifacts for every known form, not just the name that
   appeared in the final reducer plan. For example, searching only `Rob Burnett`
   can miss evidence that says `Burnett`, and searching only a handle can miss a
   full-name correction.
3. Also inspect any artifact-level smoke-check lists such as
   `people_resolver_smoke_checks`; unresolved natural names or handles should be
   treated as apply-review blockers until manually classified.
4. Discount matches that appear only inside encoded blobs, screenshots, binary
   payloads, tool command echoes, or the current review conversation. Those are
   search artifacts, not person evidence.
5. Promote only verified durable identity/contact/role/routing facts with
   `people/scripts/people_index.py upsert`, which defaults to global/user
   storage. Keep transient issue status, CI results, one-off reviews, and stale
   operational state out of the people index.
6. If an artifact mentions a person but evidence is incomplete, add only a
   minimal known-person entry after user approval, or leave a private TODO in
   the artifact review notes. Do not invent handles, roles, or relationships.

## Privacy And Portability

- Never publish private mappings, contacts, notes or profile files in public GitHub artifacts, tracked docs/examples or logs
  unless the user explicitly requests a sanitized public summary. Do not dump
  the index; surface only task-relevant fields.
- Trust hints, actor posture and bot ownership stay private: never quote them
  into public GitHub artifacts; when needed, report only their operational
  effect, such as “unknown actor; verified independently.”
- Contact details are private, not credentials; ignored people config may hold
  them for routing. Tokens, passwords, API keys, credentials, private messages
  and sensitive personal data do not belong there.
- Verify current GitHub activity before claims about recent work, comments,
  PRs or reviews. Notes are context, not live evidence.
- Consumers use context only when an index or resolver is available and continue
  normally otherwise; do not add hard skill dependencies before an explicit
  dependency mechanism exists. Soft consumers include github-plan for people
  values, memory-distillation for durable identity migration, rollout-friction
  for identity mistakes, and work rollups for subjects before live collection.

The client sent a request and didn't get the expected response within its time limit, so it gave up. The log line usually shows which phase ran out of time:

- **Connect timeout:** the TCP or TLS connection never finished. The usual causes are a host that can't be reached, a firewall or security group dropping packets, the wrong host or port, or a DNS name pointing at a dead address.
- **Read or response timeout:** the connection worked, but the server was too slow to send a response or the rest of the body. The usual causes are an overloaded or blocked upstream, a slow database query or dependency behind it, or a timeout set too low for the work.
- **Gateway timeout (HTTP 504 from a proxy or load balancer):** the proxy reached its own limit while waiting for the backend. That points at the backend, not the network between you and the proxy.

201	## Hard Gates

220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the

316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session

321

323	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
324	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
325	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
326	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
327	
328	## Friction Signals
329

196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction And Model Matrices
316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session
319	traces for durable memory/profile/local-config candidates and approves that
320	inspection. It prepares review artifacts, not memory updates.
321	
322	Before extraction or rollout/model matrix evaluation, read
323	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
324	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
325	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
326	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
327	
328	## Friction Signals
329	
330	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
331	
332	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
333	- retries of the same or very similar operation
334	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
335	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
336	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
337	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
338	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
339	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
340	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
341	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
342	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
343	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
344	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
345	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
346	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
347	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
348	- long status-polling loops
349	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
350	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
351	- repeated planning without new execution
352	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
353	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
354	
355	## Promotion Rules
356	
357	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
358	  procedural.
359	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
360	  misuse.
361	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
362	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
363	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
364	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
365	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
366	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
367	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
368	  the identity source.
369	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
370	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
371	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
372	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
373	  resolved environment noise.
374	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
375	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
376	
377	## When Not To Scout
378	
379	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
380	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
381	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
382	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
383	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
384	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
385	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
386	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
387	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
388	  Studio diagnostic pass.
389	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
390	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
391	  not public skill content.
392	
393	## Reporting
394	
395	Keep reports compact and redacted:
396	
397	- What trace source was audited.
398	- What friction signals were found.
399	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
400	- What durable destination is recommended.
401	- What changes require explicit approval.
402	- What remains unknown or risky.
403

2	
3	Read before explicitly requested durable-memory extraction or rollout/model matrix evaluation.
4	
5	- [Memory extraction](#memory-extraction-workflow)
6	- [Long-context prompt path](#long-context-prompt-path)
7	
8	## Memory Extraction Workflow
9	
10	1. Run `extract_rollout_memory.py` with explicit time/file bounds and an ignored
11	   `.local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/` output directory. Use `--trusted-originals`
12	   only for localhost or trusted-LAN models approved for private local inputs;
13	   use `--redact` for cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints. Redacted
14	   extraction strips obvious secrets, local paths, and person identifiers such as
15	   natural names, handles, and emails from candidate text and prompts.
16	2. Prefer destination-filtered passes when applying memory. Review `people`,
17	   `profile`, and `local-llm` separately from `repo-specific` and
18	   `rollout-friction` candidates so repo details do not pollute central memory.
19	3. Tune `--batch-chars` and `--max-record-chars` from a small calibration run.
20	   Oversharded prompts lose synthesis value, while overlarge prompts are more
21	   likely to truncate or omit candidate IDs. Validate with
22	   `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py` before scaling.
23	4. Use `review_rollout_memory_batches.py` only against trusted local/private
24	   endpoints. Resolve endpoint, role, model, TTL, and context through the
25	   `local-llm` skill's API-first lifecycle. For broad extraction batches,
26	   prefer `--role rollout_memory_review --load-policy api_explicit --warmup
27	   --unload-after` so the context/load parameters are explicit and the warm-up
28	   sends only harmless text before private rollout prompts. Use JIT+TTL for
29	   smaller scout passes, not broad memory-review batches. Use
30	   `--split-on-failure` when malformed or incomplete batches need deterministic
31	   child-batch retries.
32	5. Apply nothing from a batch that fails strict JSON or candidate coverage until
33	   it is rerun, split, or manually reviewed.
34	6. Run `reduce_rollout_memory_reviews.py` only after strict validation. Treat the
35	   reducer output as an apply-plan draft. Start manual review from
36	   `curated_shortlist`, then inspect full destination buckets only when the
37	   shortlist reveals a useful theme. The shortlist is advisory, not an auto-apply
38	   list; inspect suggested updates before editing `.local/profile.md`,
39	   `.local/people.yaml`, `.local/local-llm.yaml`, skills, or repo files.
40	   When the apply plan or temporary artifacts include `people_updates`,
41	   `people_resolver_smoke_checks`, visible person names, handles, aliases,
42	   reviewer/assignee/manager fields, or contact/routing notes, invoke the
43	   `people` skill's artifact review workflow before closeout: search the local
44	   artifacts for every known alias/handle form, inspect smoke checks, and verify
45	   natural names resolve before considering people-memory work complete.
46	7. For explicitly approved cloud or long-context comparison tests, use
47	   `prepare_rollout_memory_long_context_review.py` to build selected-note prompts
48	   with a `candidate_id_manifest`. Validate outputs with
49	   `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py --allow-implicit-discards`; this mode
50	   still requires every candidate in `reviewed_candidate_ids` and treats omitted
51	   reviewed candidates as implicit discards.
52	8. Use `run_rollout_memory_long_context_matrix.py --dry-run` before full matrix
53	   tests. For real approved cloud tests, pass both `--allow-private-cloud` and
54	   `--confirm-private-provider <provider>` for each provider that may receive
55	   private prompt content in that run. Capture stdout JSONL under `.local/`; use
56	   `--output-dir` for normalized per-row cloud artifacts that need later
57	   qualitative comparison. Pass `--output-jsonl` with `--skip-existing` for
58	   resumable runs. By default, resumable runs skip only existing `passed` rows;
59	   use `--skip-status` only when intentionally preserving another status, and
60	   `--retry-status` when rerunning a previously skipped status after an access
61	   window or harness fix. Treat statuses such as
62	   `prompt_too_large`, `blocked_access`, `blocked_transport`, `budget_exceeded`,
63	   `timeout`, and `failed_validation` as first-class results to retry or fix, not
64	   as successful reviews.
65	
66	## Long-Context Prompt Path
67	
68	For rollout/model matrix evaluation, use the provided scripts and their bounded,
69	provider-specific one-shot transports: `code-llm` variants use strict
70	`code llm request --message-file`. Do not use `agent.create` `context_files`
71	for rollout prompt payloads in matrix/model evaluation.
72	
73	`context_files` snapshots file contents directly into a spawned agent prompt.
74	Use it only for deliberate agent-context snapshots, with an explicit large
75	`context_budget_tokens` when a large file is intended.
76

I also loaded `shared:people` because the draft contains people fields. I ran no commands, and every command below is a plan only.

## What `batches.json` shows

| Batch | Strict JSON | Candidate coverage | Usable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `first` | ✅ | ✅ complete | Yes, after review |
| `second` | ✅ | ❌ incomplete | **No.** Nothing from it can be applied yet |

The reducer is only supposed to run after every batch passes validation, and `second` hasn't. So the current draft can't be trusted and should be rebuilt, not reviewed as it stands.

## Recovering the incomplete batch (trusted-local only)

1. **Rerun or split `second`** against the approved trusted-local endpoint:
   ```

     --split-on-failure --max-input-chars <bound> \

   ```
   - Choose the endpoint, model, TTL and context through the `local-llm` lifecycle. Don't substitute remote agents or `context_files`.
   - `--split-on-failure` retries the failed batch as smaller child batches in a repeatable way.
   - I haven't confirmed whether the script can target only `second`. If it can't, you could review the missing candidate IDs by hand instead.
2. **Revalidate** with `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py`. Every batch must show `strict_json_valid` and `candidate_coverage_complete` as true. I haven't checked that script's exact arguments, so look them up before running it.

- **Shortlist:** start with `profile-note`. It's a suggestion, not something to apply automatically. Check the proposed text before touching `.local/profile.md`.
- **People artifact review** is required because the plan has `people_updates` and smoke checks:
  1. Load the global and repo-local people indexes. Build search terms from each person's id, display name, aliases, handles, bot aliases and compact forms.
  2. Search all the new `.local/rollout-memory/<run-id>/` artifacts for every one of those forms, not just `synthetic-alias`.

  4. Ignore matches that appear only in encoded blobs, echoed commands or this conversation.
- **Output:** a proposal showing each candidate, its evidence summary and where it would go (people / profile / local-llm, kept separate from repo-specific). Any `people_index.py upsert` or profile edit needs your explicit approval for that specific change.

## If you later approve a private cloud long-context matrix

195	
196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction And Model Matrices
316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session
319	traces for durable memory/profile/local-config candidates and approves that
320	inspection. It prepares review artifacts, not memory updates.
321	
322	Before extraction or rollout/model matrix evaluation, read
323	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
324	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
325	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
326	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
327	
328	## Friction Signals
329	
330	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
331	
332	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
333	- retries of the same or very similar operation
334	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
335	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
336	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
337	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
338	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
339	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
340	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
341	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
342	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
343	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
344	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
345	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
346	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
347	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
348	- long status-polling loops
349	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
350	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
351	- repeated planning without new execution
352	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
353	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
354	
355	## Promotion Rules
356	
357	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
358	  procedural.
359	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
360	  misuse.
361	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
362	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
363	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
364	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
365	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
366	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
367	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
368	  the identity source.
369	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
370	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
371	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
372	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
373	  resolved environment noise.
374	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
375	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
376	
377	## When Not To Scout
378	
379	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
380	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
381	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
382	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
383	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
384	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
385	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
386	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
387	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
388	  Studio diagnostic pass.
389	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
390	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
391	  not public skill content.
392	
393	## Reporting
394	
395	Keep reports compact and redacted:
396	
397	- What trace source was audited.
398	- What friction signals were found.
399	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
400	- What durable destination is recommended.
401	- What changes require explicit approval.
402	- What remains unknown or risky.

None of it should be reviewed or acted on yet.

## Recovering the incomplete batch (trusted-local only)

If it still fails, review that batch by hand.
3. **Validate** with `validate_rollout_memory_llm_results.py` until both batches pass strict JSON and complete candidate coverage.
4. **Rerun the reducer** to get a fresh `apply-plan.json`. Throw away the current draft.

  - Ignore matches that only appear in encoded blobs, command echoes or this conversation.
- **Output:** a compact, redacted proposal listing, for each candidate, where it would go (profile, people, local-llm, repo-specific or rollout-friction), the evidence, and the exact `people_index.py upsert` or file edit it would need. Each of those needs your separate approval.

## If you later approve a private cloud long-context matrix

**Supported route:**
1. Build selected-note prompts, including a `candidate_id_manifest`, with `prepare_rollout_memory_long_context_review.py prepare <llm-prompts.jsonl> --budget <budget>`. If you want new extraction for a cloud run, it should use `--redact`, not `--trusted-originals`.

**Approval is separate:** approving the cloud matrix would not authorize applying any memory or people updates, and approving local review now doesn't authorize cloud transmission. You'd need to approve each one explicitly when the time comes.

196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction And Model Matrices
316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session
319	traces for durable memory/profile/local-config candidates and approves that
320	inspection. It prepares review artifacts, not memory updates.
321	
322	Before extraction or rollout/model matrix evaluation, read
323	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
324	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
325	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
326	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
327	
328	## Friction Signals
329	
330	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
331	
332	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
333	- retries of the same or very similar operation
334	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
335	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
336	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
337	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
338	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
339	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
340	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
341	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
342	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
343	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
344	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
345	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
346	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
347	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
348	- long status-polling loops
349	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
350	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
351	- repeated planning without new execution
352	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
353	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
354	
355	## Promotion Rules
356	
357	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
358	  procedural.
359	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
360	  misuse.
361	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
362	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
363	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
364	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
365	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
366	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
367	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
368	  the identity source.
369	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
370	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
371	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
372	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
373	  resolved environment noise.
374	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
375	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
376	
377	## When Not To Scout
378	
379	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
380	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
381	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
382	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
383	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
384	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
385	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
386	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
387	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
388	  Studio diagnostic pass.
389	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
390	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
391	  not public skill content.
392	
393	## Reporting
394	
395	Keep reports compact and redacted:
396	
397	- What trace source was audited.
398	- What friction signals were found.
399	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
400	- What durable destination is recommended.
401	- What changes require explicit approval.
402	- What remains unknown or risky.
403

195	
196	# Rollout Friction
197	
198	Use this skill only when the user explicitly invokes it or clearly asks to audit
199	rollout files, session traces, runout files, or agent workflow friction.
200	
201	## Hard Gates
202	
203	- Do not use this skill implicitly. If the user did not explicitly ask for
204	  rollout/session friction analysis, do not load or apply this workflow.
205	- Start in read-only mode: inspect traces, classify signals, and propose changes
206	  first.
207	- Do not edit, delete, move, archive, upload, summarize into public docs, or
208	  commit raw rollout/session files unless the user explicitly approves that exact
209	  action.
210	- Treat approval as scoped. Approval to analyze traces does not authorize skill,
211	  harness, memory, issue, repo, or local-config changes.
212	- Reconfirm approval when a proposed action changes destination. For example,
213	  approval to draft a skill change does not authorize a harness patch or local
214	  config edit.
215	- Never put secrets, credentials, private hostnames, customer/client data,
216	  private message contents, local-only paths, machine-specific values, or
217	  personal account details into public skills or repo docs.
218	
219	## Source Roles
220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is

269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an

271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly

281	   scout. When the

284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction And Model Matrices
316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session
319	traces for durable memory/profile/local-config candidates and approves that
320	inspection. It prepares review artifacts, not memory updates.
321	
322	Before extraction or rollout/model matrix evaluation, read
323	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
324	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
325	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
326	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
327	
328	## Friction Signals
329	
330	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
331	
332	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
333	- retries of the same or very similar operation
334	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
335	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
336	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
337	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
338	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
339	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
340	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
341	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
342	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
343	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
344	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
345	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
346	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
347	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
348	- long status-polling loops
349	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
350	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
351	- repeated planning without new execution
352	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
353	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
354	
355	## Promotion Rules
356	
357	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
358	  procedural.
359	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
360	  misuse.
361	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
362	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
363	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
364	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
365	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
366	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
367	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
368	  the identity source.
369	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
370	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
371	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
372	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
373	  resolved environment noise.
374	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
375	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
376	
377	## When Not To Scout
378	
379	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
380	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
381	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
382	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
383	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
384	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
385	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
386	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
387	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
388	  Studio diagnostic pass.
389	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
390	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
391	  not public skill content.
392	
393	## Reporting
394	
395	Keep reports compact and redacted:
396	
397	- What trace source was audited.
398	- What friction signals were found.
399	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
400	- What durable destination is recommended.
401	- What changes require explicit approval.
402	- What remains unknown or risky.

220	
221	- **Rollout/session files**: private short-term evidence of what happened during
222	  an agent session. They are diagnostic inputs, not durable truth.
223	- **Friction findings**: local summaries of repeated failures, confusion, tool
224	  pressure, or workflow drag. They need human review before promotion.
225	- **Skills**: public, durable agent behavior and reusable workflows.
226	- **Harness/code changes**: durable fixes when the environment can make the
227	  correct path easier or harder to misuse.
228	- **Local config**: private account, token, path, machine, or repo preference
229	  data. Prefer gitignored config for anything not safe to publish.
230	- **People local config**: when the optional `people` skill and
231	  `.local/people.yaml` are available, use them as maintained private context for
232	  identity, aliases, bot aliases, handles, contact surfaces, actor trust hints,
233	  and role hints while classifying person-related friction.
234	
235	## Audit Workflow
236	
237	1. Identify the relevant trace sources. Prefer recent, scoped rollout/session
238	   files over broad historical scans. Each host keeps its own: Codex writes
239	   rollout files under its home's `sessions` folder, and Claude Code writes
240	   transcripts under its `projects` folder. Ask for the location when it is not
241	   evident; there is no default. The helpers read both hosts' traces and
242	   classify tool outcomes, including failed results, nonzero exits, and denied
243	   commands, from each host's structured records.
244	2. Run `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/analyze_rollouts.py` with explicit paths
245	   or an explicit bounded `--root`. For many recent files, write the paths to a
246	   newline- or NUL-delimited file and pass `--paths-file`; do not pass one
247	   space-joined path string. Keep `--max-files`, total `--max-bytes`, and
248	   optional `--max-file-bytes` bounded, and read `scan_limitations` separately
249	   from findings when judging degraded scans. For long scans, use `--progress`
250	   and an optional cooperative `--max-seconds` budget; keep an outer process
251	   deadline for operations that cannot be interrupted between checks. Read the
252	   [budget and count contract](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
253	   a time-limited result. Keep analysis local.
254	3. Run `segment_rollout_episodes.py` over the same bounded source set to turn
255	   line-level signal hits into costed friction episodes. Episodes are the review
256	   unit: they preserve the intent-to-outcome shape better than individual
257	   snippets while still avoiding raw trace dumps. Read
258	   [event count semantics](references/event-counts.md) before interpreting
259	   counts, comparing reports, or supplying reports to a model. Version 2 counts
260	   command results and executed retries; other signal counts remain text
261	   matches. Nonzero exits and text hints still require human classification.
262	4. Run `cluster_rollout_episodes.py` on the episode JSONL to collapse recurring
263	   patterns into root-cause clusters and compact trajectory skeletons. Review
264	   high-cost clusters before inspecting raw trace snippets. Skeleton output is
265	   redacted by default; pass `--trusted-originals` only for approved local-only
266	   review where path/email/id shapes are useful. Treat hit counts as triage, not
267	   as proof that thousands of durable lessons exist.
268	5. When session context includes an Every Code auto-review ledger or repeated
269	   warnings about generated detached `auto-review-<hex>` worktrees, save the ledger text to an
270	   ignored local file and run `classify_auto_review_ledger.py` against the active
271	   repo. Default JSON redacts raw local finding locations and titles into stable
272	   ids; use `--trusted-local-details` only for approved local-only diagnosis.
273	   Treat `current_target` findings as review evidence to address or explicitly
274	   defer even if the review ran in a detached generated worktree. Treat
275	   `detached_auto_review` findings as external proposal history by default only
276	   when the snapshot does not match the active target; verify against active
277	   `HEAD` before letting them block the current task. Do not read, delete, or
278	   modify detached auto-review worktrees as part of this classification.
279	6. If a local LLM is useful, give it trajectory skeletons or redacted analyzer
280	   output, not broad memory-candidate batches. Use it only as a private bounded
281	   scout. When the
282	   optional `local-llm` skill is available, first resolve the endpoint locality
283	   and trust from local config or inventory:
284	   - For trusted `localhost` or trusted-LAN endpoints, original private local
285	     rollout snippets may be sent to the model for the current task. Keep the
286	     run bounded, strip obvious secrets such as tokens/passwords/API keys, and
287	     store any raw prompts or outputs only in ignored local files when needed.
288	   - For cloud, unknown, disabled, or untrusted endpoints, give only redacted
289	     analyzer output, signal names, and short synthesized observations, not raw
290	     traces.
291	     Use the model index and shared local-LLM lifecycle helper for
292	     endpoint/model selection, JIT loading, warm-up, TTL, and bounded chat
293	     mechanics, while keeping this skill's rollout-specific evidence rules. Use
294	     deep or cold-load model roles only for deliberate large-model reviews, not
295	     ordinary audits. Prefer
296	     `uv run rollout-friction/scripts/lm_studio_scout.py <redacted-report> --role rollout_scout --load-policy jit_chat --ttl 300 --warmup`
297	     when LM Studio is available. Run at most one scout pass unless the user asks
298	     for another.
299	     Ask for missing classes or false-positive patterns, then verify every
300	     suggestion yourself against maintained sources before acting.
301	7. Classify each cluster or high-cost episode as one of:
302	   - `promote-to-skill`
303	   - `fix-script-or-helper`
304	   - `fix-harness`
305	   - `move-to-local-config`
306	   - `investigate-repo-workflow`
307	   - `ignore-noise`
308	8. Verify any durable recommendation against maintained sources before proposing
309	   it. Examples: local code, skill files, repo docs, GitHub state, harness code,
310	   official docs, or config schemas.
311	9. Present a concise proposal with the cluster, evidence summary, likely cause,
312	   recommended destination, and exact changes that would need approval.
313	10. Ask for explicit human approval before making any changes.
314	
315	## Memory Extraction And Model Matrices
316	
317	Prefer the episode and cluster workflow for ordinary friction audits. Use legacy
318	broad extraction only when the user explicitly asks to mine rollout/session
319	traces for durable memory/profile/local-config candidates and approves that
320	inspection. It prepares review artifacts, not memory updates.
321	
322	Before extraction or rollout/model matrix evaluation, read
323	[memory extraction and model matrices](references/memory-extraction.md) for
324	batch/coverage validation, destination and people review, provider confirmations,
325	bounded one-shot transports, comparison variants and resumable failure handling.
326	Keep the Hard Gates above: approval is scoped by action and destination.
327	
328	## Friction Signals
329	
330	Look for concrete patterns, not vibes:
331	
332	- repeated failed commands or tool calls
333	- retries of the same or very similar operation
334	- GitHub REST or GraphQL rate-limit pressure
335	- helpers bypassed when a skill says to prefer them
336	- helper routing stalls or repeated delegation without new state
337	- local LLM scout drift, timeouts, or unbounded trace requests
338	- login/auth/account-state loops that explain apparent tool failures
339	- local config/schema drift that makes agents rediscover private setup
340	- people/identity friction such as stale handles, wrong manager routing,
341	  unknown actors, bot ownership confusion, reviewer/assignee/contact confusion,
342	  or repeated corrections about who a named person is
343	- stale IDE inspection or readiness results
344	- validation gates that start but do not reach an observable pass/fail state
345	- auto-review loops, stale worktree findings, or rejected findings recurring
346	- stale duplicate edits left in the original checkout after clean-worktree PRs
347	- worktree lock/contention or cleanup waits that block useful progress
348	- long status-polling loops
349	- status polling whose backoff grows without a state change
350	- user corrections that indicate context drift or forgotten intent
351	- repeated planning without new execution
352	- missing tool/config/dependency failures
353	- high token-growth or duplicate-item warnings when present
354	
355	## Promotion Rules
356	
357	- Promote to a skill only when the fix is reusable, public-safe, durable, and
358	  procedural.
359	- Fix a script/helper when the right path can be automated or made harder to
360	  misuse.
361	- Fix the harness when the environment can expose clearer telemetry, prevent a
362	  repeated trap, or route agents to the right tool.
363	- Move to local config when the detail is private, account-specific,
364	  machine-specific, or repo-specific but not suitable for public skills.
365	- Move durable person identity, alias, bot alias, contact, company, trust/posture,
366	  or relationship facts to people local config when that contract is available.
367	  Rollout friction may detect wrong-person patterns, but it should not become
368	  the identity source.
369	- Ignore one-off failures unless they reveal a broader workflow flaw.
370	- Treat login/auth/account-state failures as explanatory context first. Promote
371	  them only when a reusable diagnostic or safer harness state would prevent the
372	  same investigation loop; otherwise keep them in local config or ignore them as
373	  resolved environment noise.
374	- Treat local LLM scout output as a hypothesis source, not evidence. Do not let
375	  a scout choose public routing, policy, or promotion without local verification.
376	
377	## When Not To Scout
378	
379	- Skip or further bound the local LLM scout when even a trusted local prompt
380	  would include secrets, regulated data, or third-party material that should not
381	  enter model runtime/logging. For untrusted/cloud endpoints, skip when the
382	  redacted report still contains sensitive client/customer identifiers, private
383	  project names, or compliance-sensitive details.
384	- Skip the scout for straightforward findings that can be classified directly
385	  from analyzer output and maintained sources.
386	- If LM Studio is unavailable or times out, continue with analyzer output and
387	  human review. Do not retry repeatedly unless the user explicitly wants an LM
388	  Studio diagnostic pass.
389	- Prefer `uv run local-llm/scripts/lm_studio_benchmark.py --role rollout_scout`
390	  for local setup diagnostics. Benchmark results are machine-local evidence,
391	  not public skill content.
392	
393	## Reporting
394	
395	Keep reports compact and redacted:
396	
397	- What trace source was audited.
398	- What friction signals were found.
399	- What evidence supports each signal, without raw private transcript dumps.
400	- What durable destination is recommended.
401	- What changes require explicit approval.
402	- What remains unknown or risky.
403
